solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Cocktail terrace discounts partly withdrawn

indicators.note: something withdrawn is pulled back, so the letters run backwards
only part of the phrase is used, so the letters sit inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters running across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A bar sells cocktails on its terrace, but the happy-hour discounts have been partly pulled.
explanation.walkthrough: Read terRACE DIScounts backwards and SIDECAR appears.
explanation.definitionFit: A sidecar is a classic mixed drink of brandy, orange liqueur and lemon juice.

clue.text: Two sons consuming drink on isle enjoy fair

indicators.note: to consume is to take something in, so the outer letters swallow another piece

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son, taken twice
port is a fortified wine
the Isle of Man
to enjoy something is to like it

explanation.surface: Two brothers drink port on a holiday island and have a good time at the fair.
explanation.walkthrough: The Isle of Man lies in the Irish Sea. 'Fair' looks like a funfair noun but is the adjective meaning just.
explanation.definitionFit: Playing fair means behaving with the honesty and decency expected of a good sport, a synonym relation.

clue.text: Crab maybe nicely served up at top of school

indicators.note: in a down entry, one piece sitting at the top of another simply comes first
in a down clue, going up means reading the letters from bottom to top

parts.note: a tennis player who serves an ace has aced the point
a pod is a school of whales or dolphins

explanation.surface: A crab dish, nicely served, is brought up at the head table of a school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'School' looks like a place of learning but is a group of sea creatures, fitting the marine theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Crabs belong to the decapods, the ten-legged crustaceans; 'maybe' flags a crab as just one example.

clue.text: Swimmer retiring around first half of Lent

indicators.note: going around something means enclosing it, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: a retiring person is shy, or coy

indicators.note: only the opening half of the word is kept, dropping the rest

parts.note: the first half of the word, two of its four letters

explanation.surface: A shy swimmer backs away from the pool during the first weeks of Lent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retiring' looks like a reversal signal but here it is a synonym for shy; LE goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Coley is a fish, also called saithe; crosswords often call any fish a swimmer.

clue.text: Quitting when head of section's left in charge

indicators.note: something that has left is gone, so that letter is removed

parts.note: quitting a post is resigning from it

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A boss is quitting, now the section head has walked out and left someone else in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the S from RESIGNING. The surface pits quitting against being in charge, the opposite of what the answer means.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarch who is reigning currently holds power, so the word means ruling, currently holding authority.

clue.text: Two Americans going after sea monster

indicators.note: what goes after something is placed behind it in the answer

parts.note: the Med is short for the Mediterranean Sea
US and A are both abbreviations for American

explanation.surface: Two American tourists set off in pursuit of a sea monster.
explanation.walkthrough: The Americans are written first but go after MED in the answer; 'sea monster' looks like one phrase but splits.
explanation.definitionFit: Medusa is the snake-haired Gorgon of Greek myth, whose gaze turned onlookers into stone.

clue.text: Music books filling second wagon cleared out

indicators.note: to fill something is to go inside it, so one piece sits within the others

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a second
OT is the Old Testament, a set of books

indicators.note: a word cleared out has its insides emptied, keeping only its outer letters

parts.note: the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: Music books are stuffed into a wagon which is then emptied out.
explanation.walkthrough: The books go after the first letter of MOWN, a word that happens to mean cut, which is a nice distraction.
explanation.definitionFit: Motown is the Detroit record label whose soul and pop sound became a whole genre of music.

clue.text: Strip of false tin medals

indicators.note: something false is not genuine, so the letters are rearranged into another form

parts.note: the nine letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A disgraced officer is stripped of his fake tin medals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strip of' reads as removing honours; 'Strip' alone is the definition, and 'of' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: To strip down a machine is to take it apart piece by piece, a close synonym.

clue.text: Small point raised about one making delivery

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small
a peak is a pointed top

indicators.note: in a down entry, raising letters means reading them upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A small point is raised about someone making a delivery, like a courier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Delivery' suggests a courier or a birth, but here it is the delivery of a speech.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who gives an address or talk delivers a speech, so a delivery is what the orator produces.

clue.text: Clot is cut out to be a bad speller?

indicators.note: letters knocked out of place are scattered and rearranged

parts.note: the nine letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Calling someone a clot for their bad spelling seems harsh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bad speller' suggests poor spelling at school; the question mark points to someone casting evil spells.
explanation.definitionFit: An occultist practises magic and may cast wicked spells, making a punning 'speller' of the dark kind.

clue.text: Streamlined vessel at last involved in hunt

indicators.note: something involved in another is wrapped up inside it

parts.note: to hunt for something is to seek it

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter only

parts.note: the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A streamlined boat finally joins in the chase.
explanation.walkthrough: L goes inside SEEK.
explanation.definitionFit: A sleek shape is smooth and elegant, with the clean lines of something designed to move quickly.

clue.text: Heard vulgar grandee exploding over new herb supplier?

indicators.note: in a down entry, one piece over another comes above it
what is heard is spoken, so a word is taken by its sound

parts.note: kitsch is tasteless, vulgar art

indicators.note: an explosion blows things apart, scattering the letters

parts.note: taken as written
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A vulgar grandee was heard exploding over some new herbs.
explanation.walkthrough: The sound of kitsch gives the first word's letters; GRANDEE plus N is rearranged beneath it.
explanation.definitionFit: A plot where cooks grow vegetables and herbs for the house supplies fresh herbs, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Lightly oiled extremities at front of yard

parts.note: tips are ends or extremities

indicators.note: the front of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: Something like a garden tool with its ends lightly oiled, left in the yard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oiled' is slang for drunk, so 'lightly oiled' means slightly drunk, not greased.
explanation.definitionFit: Being well oiled is British slang for drunk, so lightly oiled is merely a little tipsy.

clue.text: Game youth back drinking with maiden by ship

indicators.note: whatever drinks takes something inside, so it holds another piece
going back means reading the letters from right to left

parts.note: a teen is a young person

indicators.note: one thing by another sits next to it

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for with
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over
Noah's ark was a ship

explanation.surface: A young man goes back to drinking with a girl beside a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: NEET holds W, M and ARK. Newmarket is also an English racing town, but here it is the card game.
explanation.definitionFit: Newmarket is a traditional card game of the stops family, where players bet on special cards.

clue.text: Old Italian family outside of nice doctor's practice

parts.note: the Medici were the ruling family of Renaissance Florence

indicators.note: the outside of a word is its outer shell, first and last letters

parts.note: the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: An old Italian family living just outside Nice run a doctor's surgery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nice' could be the French city, but it is just the word whose outer letters are kept.
explanation.definitionFit: Medicine is the profession and science that a physician practises in treating illness.

clue.text: Part of magazine from vehicle that's pulled atop bank

indicators.note: in a down entry, a piece placed atop another comes first

parts.note: a cart is a vehicle drawn by a horse
a ridge is a raised bank of earth

explanation.surface: A magazine article about a horse-drawn vehicle hauled up a river bank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Magazine' suggests a periodical, but it is the ammunition holder of a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: A gun magazine is loaded with rounds of ammunition, each round being one of the things it holds.

clue.text: Jack visiting school gets a stiffener in the laundry

indicators.note: a visitor goes inside the place they visit

parts.note: SCH is the abbreviation for school
a jack tar is a sailor, as is a tar

explanation.surface: A sailor visiting a school is given starchy shirts from the laundry.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition takes in 'a', so no letter comes from it; 'Jack' is a sailor, not a playing card.
explanation.definitionFit: Laundries use this powder or spray to make collars and shirts stiff and crisp.

clue.text: Gathers together scrolls periodically before night shifts

indicators.note: one piece placed before another comes first in the answer
periodically means at regular intervals, so every other letter is kept

parts.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters
evening work periods are called lates

explanation.surface: A clerk gathers scrolls together at intervals before the night shift begins.
explanation.walkthrough: In British workplaces a late is an evening or late shift, as opposed to an early.
explanation.definitionFit: To collate papers is to assemble and arrange them in order, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Sensible having Mike replaced by northern character

indicators.note: one thing replaced by another is swapped out for it

parts.note: a sensible person is mature
Mike is M in the NATO alphabet
N is the abbreviation for northern

explanation.surface: A sensible man called Mike is replaced by a character from the north.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the M in MATURE for N. 'Character' reads as a person but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's nature is their basic temperament or disposition, so the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: Fund retracted and auction reported? It may be rigged

indicators.note: something retracted is drawn back, so its letters run in the opposite direction

parts.note: a pot is a pool of money, a fund

indicators.note: a report is spoken, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: an auction is a sale

explanation.surface: A fund is withdrawn after reports that the auction was fixed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rigged' suggests fraud, but a ship's sails are rigged in the nautical sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A topsail is a sail set above the lowest one on a mast, and sails are rigged on ships.

clue.text: Sit setter alongside fellow Olympian

indicators.note: items placed next to each other are simply joined in order

parts.note: to sit for a portrait is to pose
the setter refers to themselves as I
a don is a fellow of a university college

explanation.surface: The crossword setter sits next to a fellow Olympic athlete.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Olympian' suggests a Games athlete, but it is one of the gods of Mount Olympus.
explanation.definitionFit: Poseidon, Greek god of the sea, was one of the twelve gods who dwelt on Mount Olympus.

clue.text: Easy to draw Bob briefly on part of roof?

indicators.note: cutting something short drops its final letter
in a down entry, a piece on another sits above it

parts.note: to bob down is to duck; the last letter goes
a roof is covered in tiles

explanation.surface: An artist finds Bob easy to sketch perched on part of the roof.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Draw' means sketch in the surface, but a metal is drawn out into wire.
explanation.definitionFit: A ductile metal such as copper can be drawn out into thin wire without breaking.

clue.text: Tense children in collection of cells

parts.note: T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense
a person's issue are their offspring

explanation.surface: Nervous children are locked in a block of prison cells.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tense' looks like an adjective about the children, but it is only the letter T.
explanation.definitionFit: In biology, a tissue is a group of similar cells working together, such as muscle.

clue.text: Objective of one of the military retaining power

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: to retain is to keep hold of, so the outer letters hold another inside

parts.note: martial means relating to the armed forces
P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: The goal of one soldier is to keep hold of power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Objective' reads as a noun meaning goal, but the answer takes its adjective sense, unbiased. P goes inside IMARTIAL.
explanation.definitionFit: An objective judgement is free of personal bias, so it is fair and unbiased, a synonym.

clue.text: Elderly craftsman partly manufactured material

indicators.note: only part of the phrase is used, so the letters lie within the words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: An old artisan only partly made the fabric by hand.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer spans elderLY CRAftsman.
explanation.definitionFit: Lycra is a synthetic stretch fibre, a man-made fabric used in sportswear and swimwear.

clue.text: Charlie dodging handier person with the wooden spoon?

indicators.note: someone dodging avoids being there, so that letter is missing

parts.note: something handier is closer to hand
Charlie is C in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: Charlie avoids a more practical person holding a kitchen spoon.
explanation.walkthrough: The wooden spoon is a mock prize for coming last in a British competition, so its holder finished bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: The booby prize goes to whoever finished last, so the winner of it is the one who was beaten.

clue.text: Aim to lasso core of isolated antelope

indicators.note: a lasso loops around its catch, so one piece encircles the other

parts.note: an end is an aim or goal

indicators.note: the core of a word is its middle, so only the central letters stay

parts.note: the two central letters of the word

explanation.surface: A cowboy aims to lasso a lone antelope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Aim' looks like a verb but is a noun here, a goal.
explanation.definitionFit: The eland is a large African antelope with spiral horns, the biggest of its family.

clue.text: FT's AI is changing editor's content

indicators.note: changing the order of letters rearranges them

parts.note: the seven letters to rearrange
ED is the abbreviation for editor

explanation.surface: The Financial Times's artificial intelligence is altering what the editor writes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Content' reads as a noun, material in the paper, but the definition is the adjective meaning pleased.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone content is happy with their lot, so they are pleased and fulfilled, a synonym.

clue.text: Maintain a large stage back in Glyndebourne

parts.note: taken as written
L is the abbreviation for large
a leg is a stage of a journey or race

indicators.note: the back of a word is its end, so only the final letter is kept

parts.note: the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: Keeping up a big stage at the rear of Glyndebourne's opera house.
explanation.walkthrough: Glyndebourne is an English country-house opera festival; 'stage' is a leg of a journey, not a theatre platform.
explanation.definitionFit: To maintain that something is so is to assert or claim it, often without proof.

clue.text: Good confident nurses working for professional

indicators.note: to nurse is to hold close, so the outer letters cradle another inside

parts.note: confident means sure
G is the abbreviation for good
a machine that is working is on

explanation.surface: Good, confident nurses working for a medical professional.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nurses' looks like hospital staff but is the verb, holding G inside SURE.
explanation.definitionFit: A surgeon is a qualified medical practitioner, a member of a profession, so an example.
